page.layout: One printed page. Heading block at the top centre with CAP. XIII. and an italic summary, then "Argumentatio." and "SECT. I." headings. Main text in one column below, with a woodcut initial on the first paragraph. "Status Quæstionis." heading, then a second paragraph. Left margin: two notes beside the top section and beside the second paragraph. Faint show-through and the edge of the neighbouring page are not transcribed.

main_text.head: CAP. XIII.
Sextum nostrum Argumentum adversus Meritum de Condigno, rursus ex parte Finis Secundarii, nempe vitæ æternæ, quatenus est hæreditarium donum.
Argumentatio.
SECT. I.
main_text.p: De Præ-dic. lib. 1. c. 4. [?]Cujus operis finis non est proprie merces, sed hæreditas, illud non est proprie Meritorium de Condigno apud Deum: sed boni operis finis (scilicet vita æterna) non est proprie merces, sed hæreditas: idcirco ipsum opus bonum non est proprie Meritorium de Condigno apud Deum. Adversarii, concessa Majore, ad Minorem respondent.
main_text.head: Status Quæstionis.
main_text.p: Lib. 5. de Justif. c. 12. § Atque hanc, &c.Bellarminus pro Ecclesia Romana, Certum est, inquit, Concil. Trident. sess. 6. cap. 16. docere vitam æternam filiis dari, per Christum misericorditer promissam, & simul mercedem bonis operibus fideliter ex Dei promissione missiem[?]

page.notes: Top left margin: a faint note block, partly under show-through, reads only "De Præ-dic. lib. 1. c. 4." with the rest illegible. Its reference mark in the text is not clearly visible, so the letter "b" is a guess. The mark before Bellarminus is a small circle, read as the letter "c" with some doubt. The last word of the second paragraph is blurred and only partly readable; "missiem" is uncertain. The woodcut initial is a large ornamented C, read as the start of "Cujus". Faint marks at the left top (111 and a note) and faint text in the right and left margins are show-through or the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.
